study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective controlled multicenter trial
exposure: length of stay from admission to birth
Satisfaction with the presence of midwives
satisfaction with the presence of midwives
Length of stay from admission to birth
cohort: 999 low-risk women from a larger trial of 1,238 women in Germany
finding: While midwife attendance and workload were not significantly associated with mode of birth, women who were not satisfied with the presence of midwives or who did not receive supportive procedures by midwives were significantly more likely to experience operative delivery or a caesarean.
mod_finding: While midwife attendance and workload were not directly linked to mode of birth, women dissatisfied with midwife presence or support were significantly more likely to experience operative delivery or C-section.
